facts.claim: Ord is a 6 Gyr-old K1V orange dwarf with 0.85 M☉, 0.45 L☉, and an effective temperature of 5100 K.
facts.justification: K-dwarf mass-luminosity and old, slow rotation give a stable, long-lived star; 0.45 L☉ at 5100 K is consistent with a K1V dwarf.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: Long-lived stable star gives evolution time.
Red-shifted light selects for low-energy pigments.
Low UV reduces surface DNA damage between flares.

facts.claim: Ord is a slow rotator but still produces a strong flare about once per 40 days; surface UV is about 0.35 times Earth's.
facts.justification: Old K dwarfs retain some magnetic activity; slow rotation lowers but does not eliminate flare events, and ozone attenuates the UV.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: Radiation spikes select for repair pathways.

facts.claim: The planet orbits at 0.587 AU with eccentricity 0.04, a 178-day year, and an instellation of 1.3 S⊕.
facts.justification: Kepler's third law with 0.85 M☉ gives 178 days at 0.587 AU; instellation is 0.45/0.587² = 1.3 S⊕. The semi-major axis is trimmed from the draft's 0.62 AU to keep the referee's corrected period and the accepted stellar mass consistent.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

facts.claim: Axial tilt is 21°, giving four seasons of roughly 45 days.
facts.justification: Obliquity drives seasonal insolation; a 178-day year divided into four seasons gives about 45 days each.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: Seasonal dust belts shift with tilt.
Migration and breeding time to 45-day quarters.

facts.claim: Mass is 1.15 M⊕, radius 1.05 R⊕, and surface gravity 1.04 g.
facts.justification: M/R² gives 1.04 g; the mass and radius imply a bulk density close to Earth's.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: Earth-like gravity permits large land animals.

facts.claim: Sidereal day is 31 hours.
facts.justification: Angular momentum after a late giant impact leaves a 31-hour spin without tidal locking.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: Long days create strong diurnal temperature swings.

facts.claim: One moon, Pell, has radius 0.20 R⊕, a 16-day orbit, and raises tides 1.7 times Earth's.
facts.justification: Tidal force scales as mass/distance³; a 0.20 R⊕ moon at 16 days gives about 1.7 times Earth's tide.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: Strong tides create wide intertidal zones.

facts.claim: The magnetic dipole is 1.5 times Earth's, strong enough to hold a magnetosphere.
facts.justification: A 1.15 M⊕ planet with a thin lithosphere and vigorous core convection sustains a dipole about 1.5 times Earth's.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

facts.claim: Background surface radiation is 1.5 mSv/yr, with local thorium hotspots.
facts.justification: K-star UV is low and ozone absorbs most of it; thorium-rich crust creates local hotspots.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

facts.claim: Oceans cover 45% of the surface and average 1.6 km deep.
facts.justification: A volatile-poor world after a late giant impact leaves 45% ocean cover and shallow basins.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

facts.claim: Surface pressure is 1.4 bar.
facts.justification: A CO₂ greenhouse and a thick nitrogen inventory hold 1.4 bar.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

facts.claim: Air is 76% N₂, 15% O₂, 2.5% CO₂, 6% Ar, 0.4% H₂O, and 0.01% H₂S confined to volcanic belts.
facts.justification: O₂ is biogenic; CO₂ keeps the greenhouse; Ar is radiogenic; H₂S photolyses in days and is lethal at percent levels, so it stays at 0.01% in volcanic belts.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: 15% O₂ supports fire and large aerobes.
H₂S is a local lethal hazard.

facts.claim: Sound speed is 330 m/s at 285 K; low frequencies carry for kilometres.
facts.justification: c = √(γRT/M) for a 1.4-bar N₂/CO₂ mix at 285 K gives about 330 m/s; dense air and low attenuation carry low frequencies.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

facts.claim: A 1–2 km haze of suspended hematite makes light orange and blue-poor, with low contrast and short visibility.
facts.justification: Mie scattering by iron-oxide dust removes blue light and lowers contrast; the K-star spectrum is already red-shifted.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: Red and orange camouflage is common.
Dusk and dawn are peak activity.

facts.claim: Weather includes 10–30 m/s dust storms, acid fog in rift valleys, and lightning.
facts.justification: High pressure, fine dust, and rift topography drive dust storms, acid fog, and lightning.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: Dust storms clog filters and gills.
Acid fog corrodes carbonate and metal armor.

facts.claim: Open-ocean salinity is 1.1 times Earth's, brackish lagoons 0.3 times, and brine pools 2 times; conductivity is about 1.5 S/m in brackish water and 10 S/m in brine.
facts.justification: Evaporation in arid basins and sulfide oxidation raise salinity and conductivity; seawater and brine conduct differently.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: Electric organs work in brackish water.

facts.claim: Open-sea pH is 6.5; dry basins fall to pH 4 as sulfide oxidation produces sulfuric acid.
facts.justification: CO₂ and sulfide oxidation set open-sea pH near 6.5 and dry-basin pH near 4.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: Corrosion is a constant selection pressure.

facts.claim: Heat flow is 1.8 times Earth's, with a thin lithosphere, rifts, and hydrothermal vent fields fed by radiogenic U/Th/K enrichment.
facts.justification: Radiogenic U/Th/K enrichment and a thin stagnant lid produce 1.8 times Earth's heat flow and abundant vents.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: Vent oases support chemosynthetic food webs.
Vent fields are patchy and ephemeral.

facts.claim: The crust exposes sulfides, magnetite, hematite, and Ni/Cu/Zn ores, but no native metal at the surface.
facts.justification: The surface is oxidizing and sulfide weathering destroys native metal; ore bodies remain as oxides and sulfides.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: Armor and tools depend on smelting ore.
No naturally pure metal blades exist.

facts.claim: Primary energy sources are starlight, sulfide and iron oxidation, vent heat, and salinity gradients.
facts.justification: Redox couples and geothermal heat provide multiple primary energy sources.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: Photic and vent food webs coexist.

facts.claim: Metabolism is built on Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺ and H₂S/S⁰ redox couples, with Fe-S, Cu, and Zn enzymes.
facts.justification: Fe-S clusters and metal cofactors are real biochemistry; the redox couples are thermodynamically favorable.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: Metal cofactors are essential and limiting.
Redox sensing is a primary sense.
O₂ is poison to vent obligates.

facts.claim: Primary production is red-shifted photoautotrophy in shallow seas plus chemolithotrophy at vents.
facts.justification: The K-star spectrum and shallow photic zone favor red-shifted pigments; vents provide chemical energy.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: Two primary production systems support different herbivores.
Pigment diversity tracks depth and light.
Vent and photic ecotones are rich.

facts.claim: Oxygenic photosynthesis maintains atmospheric O₂ at 15%; this is highly speculative for this world but internally consistent.
facts.justification: A 15% O₂ atmosphere needs a large biogenic source; oxygenic photosynthesis is the only plausible one, but it is highly speculative here.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: O₂ enables large aerobes and fire.

facts.claim: Free Cu²⁺ and Zn²⁺ above about 1 µM are toxic; life chelates them with metallothionein-like proteins and vacuolar crystals.
facts.justification: Free Cu²⁺ and Zn²⁺ denature proteins at micromolar levels; chelation and vacuolar sequestration are the known biological answers.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: Detox organs are a key adaptation.

facts.claim: Life builds iron-sulfide plates, intracellular magnetite chains, and magnetite-tipped teeth, but deposits only oxides, sulfides, and phosphates—never native metal.
facts.justification: Scaly-foot snails deposit FeS plates (Warén et al. 2003), magnetotactic bacteria build magnetite chains (Blakemore 1975), and chitons armor teeth with magnetite (Lowenstam 1962); none grows native metal.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: Armor, compasses, and boring teeth are biomineral.
Metal armor is heavy and costly.
No lineage grows wires or swords.

facts.claim: Electrocytes can produce about 300 V in brackish water, but the current shorts in full brine.
facts.justification: Stacked electrocytes can produce hundreds of volts; electric eels reach 860 V, so 300 V is modest but highly speculative for this world's lineages.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

facts.claim: Sinter mats precipitate and concentrate sulfide ore, but organismal smelting is fantasy; reducing ore to metal requires a kiln.
facts.justification: Biology can precipitate sulfides but cannot reduce them to native metal; vent heat can bake ore but not smelt it.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

facts.claim: Slagroot and related plants accumulate more than 1,000 µg/g Ni in dry leaves.
facts.justification: Metal hyperaccumulation above 1,000 µg/g is real in Earth plants (Brooks et al. 1977); it deters herbivores and marks metal-rich soil.

provenance.council: planet drafts + peer reviews + astrobio referee, merged by the chair (deepseek skeptic)

consequences: Acid rain mobilizes the stored metal.
